occurrences.text:
[Should-fix] src/store/apply.rs:985 — On a node with more than one non-named host kind, a parked unnamed own `seat.created` keeps PARKED_READY true while its materializer keeps re-parking it, so `apply_pass` spends every pass re-attempting it, never reaches log heads, and reports `has_more` forever. [lanes: data-migrations]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: PARKED_READY narrowed by the diff to `kind<>'named'` (apply.rs:985) while `restore_own_seat` (src/store/seats/publication.rs ~286-310) now returns HostUnavailable when `count(DISTINCT kind)<=1` fails; facts/seat.rs:62-69 maps that to `Wait{on:Host}`; `reattempt_parked` (apply.rs:1005-1017) loops `next_reattemptable`, which ignores `run.attempted`, until `run.exhausted()`, then returns true so `apply_pass` breaks before `next_ready_head`; workers.rs:1386 re-hints on `has_more` with no backoff. Not executed; chain read from source by all three seats.
  fix-shape hint: make PARKED_READY mirror the materializer's single-kind condition (or have `next_reattemptable` skip rows in `run.attempted`), plus the spike test the finding names (two-kind store, own unnamed seat.created, two passes, second `has_more=false`).

[Should-fix] src/store/seats/publication.rs:245 — Own-log restore after a wipe brings a retired named seat back as a live `unresolved` seat holding the name, so the retired seat takes the name, its live successor is held nameless, and the next resolve of the name reattaches the retired seat. [lanes: data-migrations]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: `restore_own_seat` (publication.rs ~239-290) inserts every own `seat.created` as `state='unresolved'` and never looks for a later `seat.retired`; `materialize_seat_retired` begins `if m.local_origin { return Ok(()); }`; `named_seat_apply` (resolution.rs ~740-760) selects `name=?2 AND state<>'retired'` and calls `reattach_named_seat` on an unresolved row. Design lines 418-419 say "Retire ends continuity for good". tests/store/named_restore.rs has no retired-before-restore case (its `retired` assertions at 309/338 follow a retire made after the restore).
  fix-shape hint: during own-log replay, let a local-origin `seat.retired` retire the restored row (or have restore skip a `seat.created` with a later own `seat.retired`), and add the A-created/A-retired/B-created replay test.

[Should-fix] src/host/hc/mod.rs:877; src/host/hc/mod.rs:878 — HcHost::enumerate_targets turns a failed core capture (socket gone, refused, decode error) into Ok with complete:false instead of Err, so observation takes the durable-invalidation path that ends every open binding on the core, while Health reports a causeless PartialEnumeration and reachability is marked up. [lanes: premortem, observability]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: mod.rs:877-878 `let Some(capture) = self.capture() else { return Ok(Self::unverified(..)) }`; `capture()` (~328) collapses every failure via `.ok()?`; `unverified()` sets `complete:false`. reconcile.rs `observe_and_publish`: `Err(_)` → HostUnavailable (Frozen) but `!complete` → PartialEnumeration; `is_unavailability` (ports.rs:971) excludes it; hc is Closing so `invalidate_host_observation` runs and `mark_seat_unresolved` (observation.rs ~2021-2085) ends open bindings. workers.rs ~2545 calls `mark_up` for Invalidated. Design lines 706-709 and mod.rs:36/870 say a failed hello "closes nothing"; the native Herdr path returns Err and freezes. Not executed.
  fix-shape hint: return Err (HostUnavailable, with the capture error as cause) from `enumerate_targets` when `capture()` fails, keep CompleteUnverified for the readable-but-unverified case, and add an observe_and_publish test for a refused hc socket.

[Should-fix] src/service/turn_state.rs:35 — The turn-state key is seat plus seat generation, not a per-binding identity, so two connected top-level bindings of one seat share one entry and one binding's Stop marks the pane idle while the other is mid-turn, and the wake gate then types into a running session. [lanes: correctness]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: `TurnKey{seat, generation}`; dispatch.rs:1219 builds it from `claim.binding_generation`, which cooperative.rs:645 sets to `mapping.generation` and cooperative.rs:1050 says check-ins never bump; `top_level_generations` (named_seats.rs:41) returns equal values for every binding; named.rs:271-299 reduces "every live top-level binding idle" to one shared entry; `record(Idle)` always overwrites. SA16 admits several top-level bindings per seat; design D21 says turn state is "per binding"; tests/service/turn_state.rs uses a single key.
  fix-shape hint: key the book on a per-binding identity (binding id or the hook's session id) and make the gate require every binding's entry Idle; add a two-binding test.

[Should-fix] src/cli/mod.rs:3940 — The CLI's seat lookup for a lone herdr-core Terminal site is not host-scoped: it queries by bare tN with host None, so two attached cores that both own a seated t1 make every seat-acting CLI command in either terminal fail with 'pane t1 maps to more than one seat', and when only the other core's t1 has a seat the lookup returns that foreign seat. [lanes: correctness]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: run() (mod.rs ~349-357) sets caller_pane to the bare tN; SelfMarker/SeatDefault/derive_caller arms (~3716, ~3741, ~4108) call `located_pane_seat` → `pane_seat` → `pane_seat_on(.., None, ..)` (3883); store/queries.rs:1642 applies the host filter only `if let Some(host)`. `site_capability::seats_host` (site_capability.rs:51) already returns the core socket for a Terminal but only `named_site_seat` (3989) and hook.rs:1583 use it. herdr-core ids are per core and start at t1.
  fix-shape hint: pass `seats_host(site)` into the Terminal path's seat lookup (use `pane_seat_on(.., Some(host), ..)`), and add a two-core CLI caller test.

[Should-fix] src/service/locate.rs:376 — LocateCaller's terminal candidate and the inherited-name check ignore the candidate's socket and take the first attached core answering for tN, so with two attached cores a caller in the second core's terminal is compared against the wrong core's root (cached NotAncestor refusal or wrong environ read). [lanes: correctness, premortem, simplicity-design]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: `candidate_root` matches `LocateCandidate::Terminal { id, .. }` (socket dropped; protocol/locate.rs:15 carries it), loops every `answers_terminal_ids()` host and returns the first `Ok(Some(pid))`; dispatch.locate_caller passes all_for_reads unfiltered; `inherited_name_host` (:189) `.find`s the first terminal host likewise. Design line 726 and K4 (line 64) treat two cores both owning t1 as the designed case; `HostSessions::by_locator` exists. NotAncestor is cached until the host-set epoch changes. tests/service/locate.rs has no two-core case.
  fix-shape hint: select the host by the candidate's socket via `by_locator` (and carry the socket in the inherited-name hint), falling back to the loop only when no socket is known.

[Should-fix] src/cli/caller_location.rs:143 — The diff makes every CLI child read HC_TERMINAL_ID/HC_TERMINAL_SOCKET from the process environment, but the test scrub never removes them, so the suite's result depends on whether the runner sits in a herdr-core terminal: 54 to 90 of 1309 tests fail there, against the two zsh-absence failures in a clean environment. [lanes: test-isolation-environment]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: `CallerEnv::from_lookup` chains HC_TERMINAL_ID_ENV/HC_TERMINAL_SOCKET_ENV (caller_location.rs:143, 185-186, 217-218); `SCRUBBED_PREFIXES = ["HERDR_", "CLAUDE", "CODEX", "ZDOTDIR"]` (src/test_support/isolation.rs:15) unchanged by the diff, whose doc promises the suite behaves the same inside a pane or harness session; base `git grep HC_TERMINAL` over src is empty. Seats verified the mechanism statically; the 54/90 failure counts are the scout's observed runs, not re-run by the panel.
  fix-shape hint: add `HC_` (and TMUX/TMUX_PANE, see the companion Nit) to the scrub in test_support, not per test.

[Should-fix] src/host/named/tmux.rs:221 — When the harness is itself the tmux pane process, the binding is anchored on the short-lived hook process, so the verified binding is pruned at once and the seat silently has no tmux wake. [lanes: correctness]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: `verify_walk` returns `LivenessFingerprint::of(&below.unwrap_or(record))`, the process one step below pane_pid on the walk from the subject; the subject is `peer.pid()` from dispatch.rs ~1992 (the connecting herdr-threads hook/CLI process). With `tmux new-session 'claude'` the pane process is the harness, so `below` is the hook child, which exits; `live_bindings`/`wake_armed`/`target_wake_capability` prune on `anchor.is_alive()`. Design ~561 walks "from the binding's fingerprint pid". The integration test runs under a long-lived runner.sh in a shell, so it never hits this shape.
  fix-shape hint: anchor on the harness (the binding's own fingerprint, or the first non-caller process below pane_pid), and add a test where the pane command is the harness itself.

[Should-fix] src/host/hc/mod.rs:320 — HcHost::resume_after_epoch is an inherent method, not a HostPort override, so the daemon's `port.resume_after_epoch(..)` on `Arc<dyn HostPort>` runs the trait's no-op default and HcHost's version has no caller. [lanes: simplicity-design]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: `pub fn resume_after_epoch` sits in `impl HcHost` (mod.rs:320); `impl HostPort for HcHost` (from 697) has no override; ports.rs:4394 default is `{}`; host_sessions.rs:740/816 call it on the factory's `Arc<dyn HostPort>`; main.rs:73 builds `Arc::new(HcHost::new(..))` with no wrapper; epoch starts at 1 (mod.rs:279). NamedHost (named.rs:465) and NativeCli (native.rs:1835) put it in the trait impl. No test calls the HcHost method.
  fix-shape hint: move the method into `impl HostPort for HcHost` (or add a trait forwarder like NativeCli) and add a restart-epoch test.

[Should-fix] src/cli/caller_guard.rs:98 — A verified terminal in a two-family environment gets no seat: the CLI ends with neither pane nor site and hooks return an empty outcome, so an agent in an hc terminal of a core autostarted from a Herdr pane cannot use messaging even though LocateCaller identified it correctly. [lanes: correctness]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived (refute seat voted REJECT, outvoted) / ground ✓)
  evidence: `cli_pane`: `Guard::Terminal => None`; cli::run `site = env.non_pane_locator(Cli)` is None for Ambiguous so the terminal fallback never fires; hook.rs ~4021 `Guard::Terminal => Some(HookOutcome::default())` with no diagnostic. The design's problem statement (lines 60-62) names exactly this leak as the motivating case and the Goal gives hc terminals full messaging; the "binds nothing" limit exists only in TRUST-POLICY.md:824, text the diff itself adds, and both confirming seats grepped the design and found no acceptance of it. Refute seat's point (TRUST-POLICY:824 accepted limit; design acceptance only says LocateCaller picks the root) is answered by the majority's provenance argument and the silent-outcome point.
  fix-shape hint: let a Verified terminal bind as a Terminal site (CLI and hook), or at minimum emit a user-visible message in the verified-but-unbound case so the limit is not silent.

[Should-fix] scripts/wake-e2e.py:2767 — The tmux-named wake-e2e case counts wake lines over the whole cumulative screen with no per-case baseline, so the p1 control, which runs after the p0 case on the same recipient, sees the p0 case's stale wake line and reports a wake the daemon never typed for it. [lanes: test-causality-lifecycle]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: `wake_lines = wake_count(self.screen(1000))` with `typed = wake_lines == (1 if expect else 0)`; `screen()` is `capture-pane -p -J -S -1000` (scrollback included); TMUX_CASES = (send-p0, send-p1) run in order on one pane with no history clear; the same file baselines elsewhere (`wakes_before` ~2285, `calls_before` in this case). Not run live (final review records the tmux-named cases were not run).
  fix-shape hint: take `wakes_before = wake_count(self.screen(1000))` before the send and compare the delta.

[Should-fix] src/store/local_seat_status.rs:92 — The daemon-side rule that stops a resolved seat from taking a reused target's labels (`labels_of`'s `TargetLabels::fits` filter) is pinned by no test: removing it passes the whole suite, and the CLI test that used to pin this behaviour was deleted in this diff. [lanes: testing]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: the only tests reaching `labels_of` (tests/store/remote_seats.rs ~996, ~1064) use a matching terminal `term-pane` and `incarnation: None`, so neither `fits` branch decides; the diff deleted `participant_locations_restart_and_host_failure_do_not_label_reused_targets` from tests/cli/peer_locations.rs and its replacement feeds a mock client; the ParticipantLocations call site (queries.rs:6723) is new. Scout's mutation run (filter removed, 8665 tests, only the 3 zsh failures) not re-run by the panel.
  fix-shape hint: add a store-level test for `labels_of` with a mismatched terminal and a mismatched incarnation on a resolved seat, through both `seat list` and ParticipantLocations.

[Should-fix] src/service/launch_gate.rs:89 — The launch gate's cancelled-bootstrap refusal is untested: deleting the `view.cancelled` check passes the whole suite, so no test proves a cancelled handoff cannot release its harness. [lanes: testing]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: tests/hc_handoff.rs:437 hardcodes `cancelled: false` with no knob; the only StaleAttempt assertions use `attempt_current=false` (hc_handoff.rs:623) or a canned daemon reply (tests/cli/launch_gate.rs:113); automatic.rs:1310-1311 computes `current_attempt` and `cancelled` independently, so a cancelled bootstrap with a matching attempt, matching creation and staged Send reaches Authorized without the check. Authorization path (TRUST-POLICY H3). Mutant not re-run by the panel.
  fix-shape hint: add a `cancelled` knob to the hc_handoff Gate fixture and one case asserting `refused(StaleAttempt)` with `cancelled: true` and everything else matching.

[Should-fix] src/service/host_sessions.rs:627 — Built-in NamedHost lane degradation never reaches Health or doctor, because health_entries iterates attached() and the built-in session is deliberately not in attached(), contrary to the design's lane-registration requirement. [lanes: observability]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived (spot check confirmed, promoted) / ground ✓)
  evidence: `health_entries()` maps `self.attached()`, documented "Never the built-in one"; `attach_builtin` stores only in `self.builtin` (:820); the sole consumers are app.rs:184/2608. Design "Lane registration" (~596-598) says the built-in wake lane is registered "with Health, exactly as a dialled session's lane is" and the checklist (line 1324) requires a test; the only test touching it (`no_wake_lane_for_wake_none`) calls `session.health_entry()` directly. Failures still reach daemon.log via lane_log.
  fix-shape hint: chain `self.builtin` into `health_entries()` and add the Health test the checklist names.

[Should-fix] src/cli/doctor.rs:1250 — The doctor status-source feature is dead in production: nothing populates report.hosts.agent_status, so the agent_status lines never print outside a unit test that hand-builds the report. [lanes: observability]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived (spot check confirmed, promoted) / ground ✓)
  evidence: report["hosts"] is written once at doctor.rs:1250 as {unattachable, kind_mismatch}; `agent_status_text` (:371, called at :1587) reads the never-set `agent_status`; `git grep status_rows` finds only the definition (hc/mod.rs:236) and tests/host/hc_closure.rs:208, which hand-builds the JSON. Design line 1375 and acceptance item 1408 require doctor to show the status source.
  fix-shape hint: have doctor capture each attached hc host's `status_rows()` into report["hosts"]["agent_status"] (or drop the dead text path and the acceptance claim), and make the test go through the real report builder.

[Nit] src/host/hc/rpc.rs:115 — `SnapshotResult.terminals` is `#[serde(default)]`, so an `events.subscribe` result without a `terminals` array decodes as an empty list and is published as a CoherentVerified enumeration, which begins retirement of every seat on that core. [lanes: premortem]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: rpc.rs:114-120 `#[serde(default)] terminals: Vec<HcTerminal>`; `snapshot_of` (~193) only requires an object; `is_readable` is `all()` over zero records (mod.rs:249); `enumerate_targets` then publishes `complete:true, CoherentVerified, targets: []`. Two of three seats rate it Nit: herdr-core always emits `terminals` (dc276b7 events.rs:79, per the scout), so the trigger is a future or filtered reply shape from a same-user local peer.
  fix-shape hint: make `terminals` required (Option mapped to a decode error or CompleteUnverified), since it is the sole basis of an irreversible decision.

[Nit] src/service/dispatch.rs:212 — The inherited-name refusal (M6) never runs for a herdr-core server unless that core is already attached, because a named resolve only reads all_for_reads ports and nothing attaches the core the hint names; the hint also drops the socket, so the daemon could not attach it. [lanes: correctness]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived (refute seat voted REJECT, outvoted) / ground ✓)
  evidence: `refuse_inherited_name` builds ports from `hosts.all_for_reads()` with no attach; ResolveSeat attaches only `request.host`; `HcDiscovery::scan` is called only from src/cli/hc_target.rs; `locator_hint()` sends `<stem>:tN` (caller_location.rs:393-399) so the socket is gone; tests/hc_inherited_name.rs passes the host in a slice. Severity Nit: both the reproduce and refute seats read TRUST-POLICY.md ~638 ("a pane no host answers for skips the check") as covering an unattached core, and the check is cooperative consistency only (ground seat's Should-fix noted).
  fix-shape hint: carry the socket in the hint and let the daemon attach or probe the named core on a named resolve; otherwise state in the design that the hc half of M6 applies only to already-attached cores.

[Nit] src/service/launch_gate.rs:100; src/service/launch_gate.rs:48 — The launch gate's terminal_confirms collapses a transient terminal.get or hello failure into a permanent WitnessMismatch refusal instead of continuing to poll within the deadline, so one blip kills an authorized launch and finishes the keep:false terminal. [lanes: correctness, premortem]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✗ (voted REJECT) / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: `.is_ok_and(...)` over `observe_bootstrap_target` folds HostUnavailable, StaleHostObservation and NotFound into false; `authorize` returns `refused(WitnessMismatch)` at once after `send_staged`; `observe_bootstrap` (hc/mod.rs) maps hello/terminal.get transport errors to `host_unavailable`; the shim execs only on Authorized; `terminal.run` uses keep:false. Fail-closed, one read seconds after creation, local socket; refusal text misreports an availability failure.
  fix-shape hint: retry only HostUnavailable within the remaining deadline and map it to a distinct refusal (not WitnessMismatch).

[Nit] src/host/named.rs:283; src/cli/hook.rs:4093 — wake_gate treats a recorded Idle as sufficient and consults screen_turn_running only when a key is Busy, so a missed best-effort Busy edge (sent after hook work, result discarded) lets a wake be typed into a running turn, violating delivery rule 4. [lanes: correctness, concurrency-async]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: `screen_turn_running` is read only inside `if keys.iter().any(.. == Busy)`; `screen_blocked` passes a running-turn screen and the composer reads empty during a turn; hook.rs ~4093 sends the Busy edge after `admitted_hook_outcome`, only if `deadline > now`, result discarded (`let _ =`); the code comment ("a missed edge only delays a wake") is true for Idle, not Busy. Two of three seats rate Nit: needs a lost or late Busy edge coinciding with a p0 wake; harness composers queue the typed text.
  fix-shape hint: consult `screen_turn_running` for Idle keys too and refuse on `Some(true)`; consider reporting Busy before the hook's delivery work.

[Nit] src/service/turn_state.rs:175 — `TurnStateBook::observe_screen` decides the stale-busy clear and applies it in two separate lock acquisitions, so a fresh Busy edge landing in between is overwritten with Idle. [lanes: concurrency-async]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗ (voted REJECT) / ground ✓)
  evidence: `let clear = self.with(|inner| {...});` releases the mutex, then `self.record(key, ScreenIdle, now_ms)` re-locks; the ScreenIdle arm checks only `matches!(entry, Busy{..})`, not `since_ms`. Window is two uncontended lock acquisitions and needs a 60 s stale busy with two prior clear reads; wake_gate already has a wider inherent TOCTOU.
  fix-shape hint: do the transition inside the first `with` closure.

[Nit] src/host/hc/mod.rs:733; src/host/hc/mod.rs:438 — HcHost never applies the caller's CallBudget deadline or cancellation to socket I/O, only a pre-check, so a hung core stalls request-path reads (seat labels, LocateCaller, inherited-name check) for 5 s per call, up to 15 s per host, past the stated 1 s label bound, while holding admission permits. [lanes: premortem, hot-path-perf, concurrency-async]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: `read_labelled` (:438), `target_root_process` (:733), `server_process` (:728), `session` (:420) check only `budget.cancellation.is_cancelled()` on entry; every call goes through `Self::run` bounded only by rpc.rs:27 `CALL_DEADLINE = 5 s`; dispatch.rs:148/345-352 cap the label budget at `LABEL_READ_MS = 1000`; native.rs:1329 passes the budget with a 750 ms cap. transport.rs:684 `let _ = work.await` holds permits. Two of three seats rate Nit: bounded at 5 s per call, latency only, no store turn held.
  fix-shape hint: derive each rpc deadline as `min(CALL_DEADLINE, budget.remaining())` and pass it through `with_deadline`; order `seat_labels` so one hung call does not cascade.

[Nit] src/store/topology_handoff/runtime.rs:168 — The launch-gate poll takes the store's single writer mutex and a BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction on every 20 ms poll, outside FairWriter, although the code documents the wait as holding no store turn and no writer lane. [lanes: concurrency-async]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: `automatic_launch_gate_view` calls `execute_budgeted_decision(&mut *self.writer(budget)?, ..)`; `writer()` (store/mod.rs:454) try_lock-spins the writer Mutex; connection.rs ~1149 opens `TransactionBehavior::Immediate`; launch_gate.rs `POLL = 20ms` up to 10 s; launch_gate.rs:9 and dispatch.rs:740 say "holds no store turn and no writer lane (each poll is one short read)". `launch_gate_view` is SELECT-only; a query connection exists (store/mod.rs:1912).
  fix-shape hint: run the poll's view on a query connection, or correct the two doc comments.

[Nit] src/store/seats/resolution.rs:699 — `refuse_named_seat_pane` lets the caller-supplied, unverified `occupant_bindings.locator_hint` refuse ordinary seat allocation on a pane, although TRUST-POLICY says only M9 and `seat inspect` read that hint and that it never selects, binds, moves or ends a seat. [lanes: security]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗ (voted REJECT) / ground ✓)
  evidence: resolution.rs:662 calls `refuse_named_seat_pane` on the pane-form path; :701-708 query `occupant_bindings.locator_hint` with no host filter and return TargetAlreadyOwned (M10). TRUST-POLICY.md:651 and the resolution.rs:828 doc comment say "only M9 and `seat inspect` read it", now false. M10 itself is specified (design line 488, TRUST-POLICY line 950). Same-user model: effect is a claim-driven refusal, no privilege gain; not a security floor.
  fix-shape hint: amend TRUST-POLICY.md:651 and the resolution.rs comment to list M10 as a reader and state the stale-hint limit; add a host qualifier to the query.

[Nit] src/store/apply.rs:986 — A named-seat restore parked on `wait:host` because the named row is missing is released only by a non-named host row, the opposite of what it needs, so on a tmux-only node it stays parked until an operator replay, and on a Herdr node it spins like the mixed-kind case. [lanes: data-migrations]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: `restore_own_seat` (publication.rs ~255-262) returns HostUnavailable "own named seat restore needs the named host" when no `kind='named'` row exists; PARKED_READY tests `kind<>'named'` only (base was `EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM herdr_hosts)`); ReplayScope::Startup selects by the same predicate. Trigger needs `reserve_host_id` to fail on the restoring start (app.rs:2076-2099, non-fatal). Two of three seats rate Nit.
  fix-shape hint: fix alongside the PARKED_READY finding above: release a named-restore park on the named row (per-park readiness by what the park waits on).

[Nit] src/store/seats/publication.rs:197 — A peer that materializes a named seat's `seat.created` while still on an old binary never gets the name after it upgrades, so during and after a mixed-version rollout that seat stays nameless in that peer's store. [lanes: deploy-safety]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)
  evidence: base `SeatCreatedPayload` already parses `display_name` but has no `seats.name` column; head `materialize_seat_created` has `Some(false) => {}` for an existing remote row; 0012 adds `name` with no journal backfill; `HELD_NAME_SQL` (publication.rs:384) already extracts `$.display_name`, so a backfill is cheap. Display label only, never authority.
  fix-shape hint: backfill `seats.name` for remote rows from the journal's `$.display_name` in the migration or on first upgraded apply.

[Nit] src/cli/caller_location.rs:184 — When a named caller's environment also carries HERDR_PANE_ID, locator_hint sends only the pane, so a herdr-core server that holds the name is never checked; this is exactly the environment of a core autostarted from a Herdr pane. [lanes: correctness]
  verdict: confirmed (reproduce ✓ / refute ✗-survived / ground ✓)

Rejected 3-0: N2 (design line 915) explicitly accepts loss on crash/upgrade/stop with "no wake until that binding's next hook", wake-armed bindings keep the daemon from idle-exiting, and the no_wake report is deduplicated per episode.

src/cli/mod.rs:4041 — every named-seat CLI command is a journaled ResolveSeat write. Rejected 2-1: the always-journaled resolve is deliberate (M6/M7 guards and first-use allocation run on the CLI path), most seat-acting commands already write an operations row, and the spec sets no per-command write budget; `operations` retention is a pre-existing repo-wide matter.

src/daemon/idle_exit.rs:53 — idle exit no longer kept up by a seatless attached Herdr host. src/host/named.rs:438 — no kill switch for tmux composer wake.
